JUDGMENT & ORDER (CAV)
(Judge D, J)
1.      Heard Mr. Advocate K, learned Standing Counsel for the appellants and Mr.
Advocate J, learned counsel for the respondent.
2.      The facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent was appointed as a
Lower Division Assistant in the year 2009 and was denied the benefit of the
revised pay under Section 3 of the Assam Services (Pay) Act, 2017.
3.      Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the learned Single Judge erred
in directing the release of the arrears without considering the financial
implications. He relies on State of Assam v. Party K reported in (2015) 4 SCC 123.
4.      Learned counsel for the respondent contends that the claim is covered by the
decision in Party L vs. Union of India, AIR 2010 SC 456 and 2018 (3) GLT 789.

<FF>Page No.# 3/4
5.      The question that arises for consideration is whether the respondent is
entitled to the revised pay from the date of his appointment.
6.      We have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and
perused the materials on record. Section 3 of the Assam Services (Pay) Act, 2017 and
Article 14 of the Constitution of India are relevant. The view in (2015) 4 SCC 123 is
followed.
7.      The learned Single Judge has rightly appreciated the facts. The appellants
cannot deny the benefit to the respondent on the ground of financial burden alone.
8.      In view of the above, the appeal is partly allowed. The State appellants are directed
to release the arrears of the revised pay to the respondent within 3 (three) months
from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
9.      There shall be no order as to costs.

<FF>Page No.# 4/4
